Name the folder and affected assets.
Same task, new tester: identify scope unaided.
What is observed? What is inferred?
notes:
A preference is a starting point, but a usable finding names what happened and how it affected the task. The explanation is tentative. Maybe the label caused the pause, or maybe the task setup was unclear. Change one relevant thing and retest. Record strengths with the same care: a tester finding the target without help is evidence of a successful interaction. If no issue appeared, say that instead of inventing one.

title: Events and observation answer different questions
text: Events and observation answer different questions
Did it complete, and how long did it take?
Where did the user hesitate or need help?
Frequency across the whole user population
Which evidence would help explain a slow task in your tool?
notes:
Telemetry can record operation counts, durations and reasons for blocked actions. Observation can reveal hesitation, workarounds and misunderstanding. Combine them when useful, but do not equate a click count or successful call with a good experience. Collect only fields needed for the question and avoid copying project paths or user content unnecessarily. For this class, a short observation record is enough; we are not adding a telemetry implementation requirement.

Prepare one bounded task that a peer can attempt. We will rotate owner, tester and observer, then apply the same lens to our own tools. A useful result is an observation and a revision with a specific retest.

title: Prepare one task a peer can attempt
text: Prepare one task a peer can attempt
Expected look + correct slot + protected scope
Give a goal, not a list of clicks.
notes:
Use the preparation page to give the tester a bounded task. State the input, goal, visible success and protected scope, then let the tester choose the steps. Include a repeat or fallback method. If the tool cannot run, use a recording, paper or Figma walkthrough and label execution as untested. Do not count a walkthrough as proof of engine behavior. We will keep the same starting state and version within the review so observations can be compared.

title: Three roles, three seven-minute rounds
text: Owner: state the goal. Tester: attempt. Observer: record evidence and help.
Each tool gets one observed attempt with two peer perspectives.
notes:
Form groups of three and choose A, B and C. Each round focuses on one tool. The owner explains the goal and prepared input, then watches. The tester tries the task and says what they expect. The observer records the visible evidence and any coaching. Rotate so each person owns, tests and observes once. This is one observed attempt per tool, not three independent tests of every tool. If a group has an extra member, they can observe without inflating the number of distinct attempts.

title: One round produces evidence and a retest
text: One round produces evidence and a retest
Owner states task, input and success
Write a retest; reset and rotate
Blocked? Label the fallback mode and continue.
notes:
Keep the attempt long enough to observe meaningful behavior. Record help rather than hiding it. If setup fails, allow one brief recovery attempt, then switch to the prepared walkthrough. Use the final minute to specify the retest and reset, not to start another feature. The timer will stop at the end of the round; choose the next round deliberately. What questions do you have about the roles or the review mode?

title: Choose a revision supported by evidence
text: Choose a revision supported by evidence
Keep one strength a peer actually observed.
Prioritize one issue or uncertainty by its consequence.
State the change or investigation you will try.
Specify the retest: input, action, expected result and protected scope.
What changed or strengthened your original judgment?
notes:
Apply the same checklist to your own tool for four minutes, then use the final three minutes to record a revision and retest. A serious failure can matter even if only one person sees it. A proposed visual change remains a hypothesis until you test it. Record which mode you used, what was observed and what remains untested. Keep one observed strength so improvement does not remove behavior that already supports the task.
